name: Chip supply
value: US licence rule for 5 chip-diversion states
summary: US on 16 Nov required licences for advanced AI chips to five countries to curb diversion to China; no TSMC stoppage
state: On 16 Nov the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security required export licences for advanced AI chips shipped to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, aiming to stop Chinese firms reaching them through overseas data centres (Reuters via bdnews24; Al Jazeera, 17 Nov). Singapore said it is studying the measure. Mature-chip bottlenecks for carmakers reported at Electronica on 9–10 Nov persist. No TSMC or Samsung output disruption was found, so new controls keep Watch.
for_you: New licence requirements can slow shipments of high-end chips and AI computing capacity in Southeast Asia. Tight mature-chip supply mainly affects carmakers and industrial equipment makers, with possible delays to some vehicle and electronics deliveries.
rubric_hit: Watch: new export controls (US licence rule for advanced chips to 5 countries, 16 Nov); no major TSMC/Samsung disruption

sources.title: Al Jazeera — US moves to block China's remote access to AI chips amid Nvidia scandal
bdnews24 (Reuters) — US to curb China's access to AI chips

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
